pass1.sentence: NICE defines hyperuricaemia as a serum urate of 360 micromol/L or more.
pass1.note: Search summary of NICE NG219 evidence: hyperuricaemia defined as serum urate 360 micromol/L (6 mg/dL) or more. Barnsley/Bucks documents say the same.

pass1.sentence: Its general treatment target in gout is below 360 micromol/L, with below 300 micromol/L suggested for people with tophi, chronic gouty arthritis or ongoing frequent flares despite a level below 360;
pass1.note: NICE NG219: default <360; lower <300 for tophi, chronic gouty arthritis, flares despite <360.

pass1.sentence: the British Society for Rheumatology recommends an initial target below 300 micromol/L for everyone starting urate-lowering treatment.
pass1.note: Search summary of PMC10809909 (BSR vs NICE): BSR initial target below 300 for all. Attribution to that article is inferred from the title.

pass1.sentence: Supports gout, but the level can be normal during an attack, so it is often repeated at least two weeks after the attack settles
pass1.note: Bucks: often normal during attack, repeat 4-6 weeks after; Tayside: 4 weeks.
